Build a Medabot

Pick any head, arms and legs from either series. The pickers are the portrait sprites. The stage stacks the regular sprites, which all share one camera, so every layer is drawn at 0,0 and lands where it belongs on any bot. R picks a random build, M mixes the two series, F flips the facing.

Catalogue

Two series, one set of rules. Series 1 is the first 22 bots. Series 2 adds 22 more Medabots Infinity rips. Both share the scale, the neck point and the camera, so parts mix freely across the two.

Why the regular sprites look mostly empty. They are layers, not icons. All 44 bots and all their parts go through one camera, which is frozen, so a part keeps its place on the canvas and any head sits on any legs with no offsets. Stacking a bot’s own layers reproduces its full-body sprite with a worst-case alpha error of 0.00%. Up to 8.4% of pixels differ in shade, because a part rendered alone gets no shadow from the part next to it. trimRect in the manifest gives each layer’s tight box, for an atlas that wants to pack them.

One game scale, one neck. The rips share one scale, so every bot keeps its in-game size relative to Tinpet (Male). Compared with the old rule, which stretched every bot to one height, Spidar shrank the most and Saldron grew the most. Each bot is then moved whole so the point where its head meets its body lands on Tinpet (Male)’s neck, so any head seats on any body. Feet do not share one floor (they sit between -39 and +37 cm of Tinpet’s), and shoulders keep their own anatomy: arms land a median 9 cm from another bot’s shoulders.

Three parts: head, arms, legs. Legs means everything below the head that is not an arm: torso and legs together, which the rips deliver as one mesh anyway. The head is kept as the source game cut it, which on several bots runs down through the chest armour or includes a neck piece.

Arms are one part, three sprites. From a 3/4 view one arm is usually behind the body and the other in front of it, so no single layer can sit at one place in a draw order. The stage draws arms_back and arms_front separately. Where the back arm goes is measured from each bot’s own full render. On Arcbeetle, Knight Armor, Metabee, Potatobug, Rhinorush, Saldron, shoulder-mounted weapons put even the far arm in front of the body. A mixed build uses the slot of the bot the arms came from.
